title: CPEC Protocol
author: N.J. Hillson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6t7hern

steps.title: Measure DNA concentrations
steps.instruction: Determine the concentration (ng/ml) of each assembly piece using an appropriate method (e.g., spectrophotometer or fluorometer).

steps.title: Prepare CPEC assembly mix
steps.instruction: In a tube combine: 100 ng linearized vector backbone, equimolar amounts of each additional assembly piece, 5 ml 5X HF Phusion Reaction Buffer, 1 ml 10 mM dNTPs, 0.75 ml DMSO, 0.5 ml Phusion Polymerase (2 U/ml), and add deionized water to bring the total volume to 25 ml.

steps.title: Run CPEC thermocycler program
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler as follows: initial denaturation 30 s at 98 °C (1 cycle); then 10 s at 98 °C, 30 s at 55 °C; repeat 1–15 cycles (the number of cycles should exceed the number of assembly pieces) with each repeat cycle containing an extension of 15 s per kilobase of the assembled product at 72 °C; finish with a final extension of 10 min at 72 °C (1 cycle).

substeps.instruction: 1–15 repeat cycles (≥ number of pieces) – 15 s per kb at 72 °C

steps.title: Transform and verify assembly
steps.instruction: Transform 5 ml of the completed assembly reaction into 100 ml of competent E. coli cells, then recover or plate as appropriate; alternatively, run a diagnostic agarose gel to check for successful assembly.
